title: Release 0.11.2: two defects that were known and unfixed
body:
## Summary

`v0.11.1` is tagged at `4d83437` and `package.json` still reads `0.11.1`, so this is a bump-then-tag release. One commit has landed since:

| Commit | Issues | What it fixes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `5b1c89b` | #210, #258 | `getProductsWithSkus` forwards `fields` and `filter`; an exclusion entry can name an option or specification by `key` |

## Resolution analysis: why 0.11.2 and not 0.12.0

Both changes are additive and nothing already working changes.

- **#210** adds two optional options to `getProductsWithSkus`. A caller passing neither gets exactly today's behaviour.
- **#258** adds `key` as a fourth matchable field on an exclusion entry. An entry written before it carries no `key`, so nothing already configured changes - and `name`, `entityId` and `erc` deliberately still do **not** reach `item.key`, which is asserted rather than described. Making `name` match `key` would have altered filtering for every configuration in place; that was rejected as a behaviour change dressed as a bug fix.

The precedent is settled: v0.8.20 shipped the entire `*Page` and `collectAll` convention as a patch, and this repository reserves the minor for breaking (#221 for 0.9.0, #243 for 0.10.0, #252 for 0.11.0, #256 for 0.11.1).

## Why these two were batched

They should have gone out with 0.11.1 and did not, which cost consumers a bump. #258 was identified while exporting the item shape for #254 and left as "a decision rather than a fix"; #210 had been closed on 2026-09-10 with its fix never landed. Batching them here is the correction, so this is one further version rather than two.

Worth recording about #210: the issue was **closed as though resolved while `main` still had the defect**. `getProductsWithSkus` still took only `{catalogId, pageSize}`, so `getProducts`' default projection of `productId,externalReferenceCode,name` applied and no caller could widen it. The fix existed only on an unmerged branch, which is why that branch survived the repository cleanup - it was the sole copy. A closed issue is not evidence of a fixed defect.

## Implementation plan

1. Branch `chore/release-0.11.2`; bump `package.json` to `0.11.2`. Nothing else encodes the version.
2. Gates: `yarn test`, `yarn lint`, `yarn validate`.
3. Open the bump PR closing this issue, and stop for a human merge.
4. After the merge: annotated tag `v0.11.2`, then a GitHub release leading with the product projection, since that is the one a consumer is most likely to be hitting today.

No registry publish; consumers pin by git tag.

## Not in this release

**#3** - the PIM adapter, still blocked on a `headless-pim` spec that exists nowhere. It is the only open issue in the tracker.
